title: State of AI Identity Licensing 2026 primary-source dataset
scope: A bounded review of primary sources that directly address digital replicas, AI likeness permission, advertising disclosure or synthetic-media provenance. It is not a census of every law or contract.

version_history.change: Initial release with 12 primary sources, eight operating controls, methodology, JSON and CSV distributions.
Added the enacted TAKE IT DOWN Act and SAG-AFTRA interactive digital-replica guidance, and updated C2PA from specification 2.2 to 2.4.
Replaced the superseded 2025 NO FAKES proposal with S.4591, recorded its committee advance and the September 30 floor objection, and rechecked the C2PA 2.4 and UK digital-replica sources.
Added enacted New York rules for digital-replica contracts and synthetic performers in advertising, plus the 2026 EU AI Act amendment on non-consensual intimate material and consent safeguards.

controls.label: Permission
controls.definition: The source addresses authorization, consent, licensing or a right to control use of a person’s voice or visual likeness.

controls.label: Specific scope
controls.definition: The source addresses intended-use specificity, contract form, project limits or a requirement for additional approval.

controls.label: Compensation
controls.definition: The source addresses payment, wages, residuals, benefit contributions or disclosure of a paid relationship.

controls.label: Asset control
controls.definition: The source addresses access, security, storage, transfer or destruction of a replica or source asset.

controls.label: Disclosure
controls.definition: The source addresses telling an audience that content is synthetic, manipulated, sponsored or otherwise materially connected.

controls.label: Provenance
controls.definition: The source addresses machine-readable origin, history, marking, binding, watermarking, detection or signed content assertions.

controls.label: Lifecycle
controls.definition: The source addresses duration, expiry, termination, additional use, credential revocation or treatment after a permission period.

controls.label: Remedy
controls.definition: The source addresses unenforceability, liability, removal, a cause of action or a policy proposal intended to close a legal gap.

sources.status: Policy report and recommendations, not enacted law
sources.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 1: Digital Replicas
sources.finding: Recommends a federal digital-replica right and says licences should use informed consent, full disclosure of intended uses and limited terms.

sources.status: Enacted, applicable to specified new performances fixed on or after January 1, 2025
sources.title: AB 2602: Contracts against public policy, digital replicas
sources.finding: Makes a covered contract provision unenforceable for specified new digital-replica performances when intended use is not reasonably specific and the individual lacks the representation described by the statute.

sources.title: AB 1836: Use of likeness, digital replica
sources.finding: Adds liability for producing, distributing or making available certain unauthorized digital replicas of deceased personalities in expressive works, subject to listed exceptions.

sources.status: Enacted as Chapter 581 of the Laws of 2024; effective January 1, 2025 for contracts entered into or modified on or after that date
sources.title: S.7676-B: Contracts for the creation and use of digital replicas
sources.finding: Makes a covered digital-replica provision void and unenforceable when it lacks a reasonably specific intended use and the individual lacks the legal or collective-bargaining representation described by the law.

sources.title: ELVIS Act, Public Chapter 588
sources.finding: Adds voice, including a readily identifiable simulation, to Tennessee’s protected personal rights and extends liability to specified unauthorized uses and distribution.

sources.status: Advanced by the Senate Judiciary Committee by voice vote on June 18, 2026; a September 30 unanimous-consent request was blocked; not enacted as of October 13, 2026
sources.title: S.4591: NO FAKES Act of 2026
sources.finding: Would create a federal right in an individual’s voice and visual likeness, with a notice-and-counter-notice framework and enumerated speech protections. It remains proposed legislation.

sources.status: Enacted as Public Law 119-12; the covered-platform notice-and-removal requirement took effect May 19, 2026
sources.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act, Public Law 119-12
sources.finding: Creates a narrow federal rule for nonconsensual intimate depictions, including defined digital forgeries, and requires covered platforms to operate a notice-and-removal process. It is not a general commercial likeness-licensing statute.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 50
sources.finding: Requires certain providers to mark synthetic outputs in a machine-readable and detectable format and certain deployers to disclose deepfake image, audio or video, subject to the regulation’s exceptions.

sources.status: Enacted regulation; the new prohibitions concerning non-consensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material apply from December 2, 2026
sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Digital Omnibus on AI
sources.finding: Adds a narrow prohibition covering specified AI systems that generate or manipulate realistic non-consensual intimate material and requires appropriate safeguards to support reliable collection and demonstration of consent in the cases the regulation describes.

sources.status: Government report with a separate digital-replicas consultation announced
sources.title: Report on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
sources.finding: Says replicas can imitate a person’s voice or likeness without permission, identifies gaps in existing protection and announces further consultation rather than a completed licensing rule.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence under the 2025 Commercials Contract
sources.finding: Describes consent for creation and use, a separate clear writing, reasonably specific intended use, added consent beyond scope, compensation, access security and storage limits.

sources.jurisdiction: Covered United States television and theatrical work
sources.status: Collective agreement with some phased provisions
sources.title: 2026 Theatrical and Television Memorandum of Agreement
sources.finding: Addresses consent, payment, legitimate-business-need access, security, transfer obligations and use-specific treatment for digital replicas, with some terms phased to later dates.

sources.title: Interactive Digital Replicas and Consent
sources.finding: Describes separate written consent, a reasonably specific intended use, per-game compensation and rules allowing performers to suspend consent for generating new material during a strike.

sources.title: FTC Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
sources.finding: Says endorsements must be honest and not misleading and that unexpected material connections affecting evaluation should be disclosed clearly and conspicuously. It does not grant likeness permission.

sources.status: Enacted as Chapter 617 of the Laws of 2025; effective 180 days after December 11, 2025
sources.title: A.8887-B: Disclosure of synthetic performers in advertising
sources.finding: Requires a conspicuous disclosure when a covered commercial advertisement knowingly uses a synthetic performer, with listed exceptions and civil penalties. The defined performer is not recognizable as an identifiable natural performer, so the law does not itself establish likeness permission.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: NIST AI 100-4: Reducing Risks Posed by Synthetic Content
sources.finding: Reviews provenance, watermarking, labeling, detection, testing and auditing approaches for synthetic content. Those techniques do not establish a person’s permission by themselves.

sources.publisher: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
sources.title: C2PA Content Credentials specification 2.4
sources.finding: Defines signed, cryptographically bound assertions about an asset’s provenance and adds repository receipts plus current soft-binding and live-video mechanisms. Validation does not decide whether a depicted person consented.
